discovery: Room-temperature and giant tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions, including crystalline MgO barriers

nominees.name: Stuart S. P. Parkin
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Microstructure Physics, Halle, Germany

nominees.name: Shinji Yuasa
nominees.affiliation: National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology (AIST), Japan

motivation: In 1995 Miyazaki demonstrated large tunnel magnetoresistance (TMR) at room temperature in amorphous Al-O junctions, turning a low-temperature curiosity into a usable effect. In 2004 Yuasa and Parkin independently realised giant TMR using crystalline MgO(001) barriers, confirming the predicted coherent, symmetry-filtered tunnelling of Bloch states and reaching magnetoresistance of several hundred percent. This is a clear case of material design opening new physics: choosing the barrier crystal, not just its thickness, controls spin-dependent transport. The impact is enormous. MgO junctions replaced GMR read heads in essentially all hard disks, and they are the core element of spin-transfer-torque MRAM now in commercial production, as well as of new sensors and proposed neuromorphic devices. Giant magnetoresistance was recognised in 2007; tunnel magnetoresistance is the distinct quantum-mechanical successor that actually carries today's data storage and nonvolatile memory.
